verification.note: Recheck of 18 Oct 2026: re-read the Florida Senate bill page for HB 1159 (2026), the House Judiciary Committee analysis of CS/HB 1159 and the House final bill analysis of CS/CS/HB 1159 (1 Apr 2026), all stored from flsenate.gov on 14 Oct 2026 and found unchanged by the archiver on 17 Oct 2026. The bill page confirms the title, sponsors, history, the 105-0 House and 37-0 Senate votes, approval by the Governor on 31 Mar 2026, Chapter No. 2026-20 and the 7/1/2026 effective date; the final analysis confirms approval, chapter and effective date and describes the enacted provisions, including section 9 on generated child sexual abuse material, on which the summary rests. The staff analyses state that they are not an official statement of legislative intent, and the enrolled bill text was not stored. That s. 827.072 was created in 2024 by CS/CS/SB 1680 (ch. 2024-118) rests on the Senate Judiciary analysis and bill page stored for US-FL-03. That the act is in force rests on its 1 Jul 2026 effective date and the absence of any later change in the stored files.

summary.quote: Replaces the term “child pornography” with “child sexual abuse material” throughout Florida statutes;
Creates a life felony for aggravated use of a child in a sexual performance when a child is under 12;

summary.locator: page 2, Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
summary.quote: The bill increases the penalty for creating generated child sexual abuse material from a third degree felony to a second degree felony.

summary.locator: page 2, Generated Child Sexual Abuse Material
summary.quote: Any person in any jurisdiction other than Florida knew or reasonably should have known that he or she was transmitting generated child sexual abuse material to any person in Florida. (Section 9)

modified by electronic, mechanical, or other computer-generated means to portray a fictitious person, who a reasonable person would regard as being a real person younger than 18 years of age, engaged in sexual conduct.

notes.quote: Prohibits a person convicted of specified sexual offenses involving animals from owning or working or volunteering with an animal for at least 5 years.

judgment.status_reasoning: The Governor approved the act on 31 Mar 2026 (ch. 2026-20, L.O.F.) and it took effect on 1 Jul 2026 under section 24, per the final bill analysis and the bill page's 7/1/2026 effective date. Today, 18 Oct 2026, is after that date, and no stored file shows a later amendment or repeal; 'In force' stands.
judgment.scope_reasoning: An omnibus sexual-offences act, not AI-specific; included with the existing scope_note because section 9 raises the penalty for creating computer-generated child sexual abuse material and creates an offence of transmitting it (AGENTS.md section 10: a law that is the operative instrument for a deepfake question).
judgment.date_reasoning: date_published is the Governor's approval, 31 Mar 2026; date_in_force is the 1 Jul 2026 effective date. Chapter No. 2026-20 was recorded on 1 Apr 2026 (in the bill page's last action), which is not an adoption date.
judgment.summary_reasoning: The current summary matches the final bill analysis: the terminology change, the higher penalties and mandatory minimums, the life felony for a child under 12, the higher penalty for creating generated material and the new transmission offence (Section 9), and the definition of generated material that s. 827.072 keeps. Left unchanged.
